messages:
sam-support: Customer (Jordan) reports streaming cutoff after ~45s idle, then client reconnects and gets partial/duplicated final chunk, sometimes 401 on reconnect.

jordan (customer-jordan): repro attached, happens on ALB fronted by Cloudflare. App server logs show final event sent, client sees truncated chunk and connection close.

sam-support: Key facts: 1) Long idle (>30s) 2) Using ALB with default idle timeout 60s 3) Cloudflare in front with HTTP/2 to client, HTTP/1.1 to origin 4) Token-based auth with short-lived JWT renewed on reconnect.

mira-eng: Can you paste the minimal curl repro?

sam-support: here's the curl command Jordan used:

``
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.customer.example/v1/stream?model=x"
``

sam-support: They used --no-buffer (-N) and saw initial events, then silence, then reconnect. On reconnect the client got a 401 about 2s after TCP reestablished.

tyler-sre: Do we have tcpdump from the proxy/ALB side? Need to confirm FIN/ACK or RST pattern.

cleo-obs: Ill grab traces now. (pulling logs)

cleo-obs: Observability notes: origin log shows last chunk written at 12:03:21. ALB connection to origin closed at 12:03:22 (idle-timeout). Client reconnected from same client IP at 12:03:24, new TLS session negotiated via Cloudflare.

cleo-obs: Origin returned 200 on first connect, then on reconnect origin returned 401 because token in reconnect request was short-lived and expired between attempts.

cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare note: when HTTP/2 multiplexing to client and HTTP/1.1 on origin, Cloudflare will re-establish connections to origin as needed. Idle connection reuse settings may close earlier than client expects.

mira-eng: So symptoms: origin sends final chunk, ALB idles and closes backend connection; client still has open HTTP/2 stream, then client reconnects sending new request with refreshed token but Cloudflare replays to same origin connection token vs new? Could be cookie/connection pooling reusing stale auth? Need to check if Cloudflare strips/merges Authorization header when reusing pooled connection.

tyler-sre: Also seen cases where ALB half-close triggers a truncated chunk delivered to client when edge coalesces buffered chunk + FIN. We should capture bytes on the wire around the idle close.

sam-support: Jordan provided pcap snippet. Paste:

``
12:03:21.123 IP client > cloudflare: TLS AppData (len=512)
12:03:22.001 IP cloudflare > alb: TCP FIN
12:03:22.002 IP alb > origin: FIN ack
12:03:24.010 IP client > cloudflare: TLS ClientHello (new conn)
12:03:24.100 IP client > cloudflare: TLS AppData (request, Authorization: Bearer <new_token>)
12:03:24.200 IP cloudflare > origin: GET /v1/stream  (pool id reuse)
12:03:24.202 IP origin > cloudflare: 401 Unauthorized
``

mira-eng: That line "pool id reuse" stands out — origin saw a GET on an existing socket where cloudflare sent the new request but origin treated session as new and validated token and returned 401. Hmm.

tyler-sre: Potential cause: Cloudflare may reuse keep-alive socket to origin but not forward updated Authorization header in some rare code path? Unclear.

cleo-obs: I inspected the full origin request headers seen by us on that socket: the Authorization header was present and had the new token value. So Cloudflare did forward it.

mira-eng: Then why 401? Check auth service logs — maybe token issuer invalidated tokens for that client when idle detected, or token clock skew. Also check NTP on origin.

sam-support: Jordan says tokens are 60s TTL. They refresh on reconnect. Reconnect occurs ~2-3 sec after the ALB closed.

tyler-sre: Another vector: ALB sets PROXY protocol or x-forwarded-for changes and auth server expects consistent client fingerprint. If connection came from different source port after LB rebind, auth mapping fails.

cleo-obs: Auth logs show "signature mismatch" not token expired. So token was altered or truncated en route. Look at header length; sometimes ALB truncates large headers when reusing connection after close.

sam-support: Jordan's header sizes are normal (Authorization ~200 chars). Not huge.

mira-eng: Could be HTTP/1.1 to origin path causing downstream connection reuse mismatch with keep-alive + half-close. Some proxies, when reusing socket that recently had FIN, append buffered bytes incorrectly, leading to a malformed auth header and 401 signature error.

tyler-sre: Repro plan: 1) Increase ALB idle timeout to 300s for a customer environment to see if disappearance stops 2) Enable TCP keepalive on origin side and ensure we gracefully drain 3) Add additional logging to auth service to dump Authorization header raw on failure (redact tokens) 4) Ask CF to disable connection pooling for this origin as an AB test.

sam-support: Jordan is okay with a short config change. Implementing ALB change now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: change-alb-idle-300 for customer-788 cluster (rollout 1/3)

cleo-obs: After ALB idle timeout bumped, Jordan ran the same repro. Result: stable stream, no reconnect 401 after 15m test. :tada:

mira-eng: Good signal. Next steps: root cause still ambiguous — need to confirm whether the issue is race between ALB closing and CF pooling. Recommend issuing a test where ALB kept at 60s but CF origin pool disabled to isolate.

tyler-sre: Also recommend code hardening: server should treat reconnections idempotently and not rely on socket-level continuity for auth mapping. If header malformed during early close it should return 400, not 401 signature.

sam-support: Noted. Jordan will keep ALB change for now; we will follow up with CF support case to request deeper origin connection tracing.

mira-eng: I'll open a Cloudflare ticket and include pcap + origin logs. FYI I'll ask them to check early socket half-close + header framing.

sam-support: Thanks all — documenting final workaround and steps in the support case. Closing for now but leaving thread open for CF updates. :white_check_mark:

jordan (customer-jordan): Thanks everyone — huge help, service is stable now.
